Decision models, facts and expression language

A source-linked technical walkthrough with an executable-system perspective.

After this session, you can:
  • Read a model contract
  • Distinguish missing, invalid and false
  • Design explainable outcomes

Technical flow

1. Typed facts

Models declare the facts they accept, their types and validation constraints. Money and ratios cross JSON boundaries as strings so parsing is explicit and floating-point ambiguity never enters evaluation.

2. Expression semantics

The expression language supports bounded deterministic operations with defined comparison, boolean and missing-value behavior. Unknown functions or malformed operands invalidate evaluation rather than producing a permissive guess.

3. Outcomes and reasons

Models return domain outcomes such as approve, refer, decline, allow, deny or require_human with stable reason and trace information. Explainability comes from evaluated policy structure, not generated prose.
